listenings.text: Okay, everyone, come closer to the fire. When I was your age, my family used to come here every summer. We didn't have a van. We used to drive down in a tiny old car, with the boards on the top and the tent in the back. We used to sleep in a tent in the forest, and we cooked fish on a campfire every night. Back then it was a quiet town. Most people used to work on farms, and there weren't any cafes. My dad used to say, if you see three cars at the beach, it's crowded. Nowadays it's very different. There are cafes and wineries everywhere, and a lot of tourists in summer. And every year the best surfers in the world come here for a big contest. But the waves are the same. Big, cold and beautiful. Now, go to bed. Your first heat is tomorrow.

Can I tell you a secret, mate? When I was a grommet, I used to be scared of big waves. Really scared. On big days I used to sit on the sand and just watch. I used to surf with my older brother, on his old longboard, because I didn't have my own board. And I didn't use to eat breakfast before a heat. I used to feel sick. Nowadays it's different. I still don't eat a lot before a heat, but I stretch, I listen to music, and I feel ready. So if you've got butterflies tomorrow, that's normal. Everybody does. Okay. Good night.

reading.rtitle: Welcome to Margaret River: Then and Now
paras: Fifty years ago, Margaret River used to be a quiet farm town. Most people used to work on farms or in the big forest around the town. There weren't many shops, and there didn't use to be any cafes. On a Saturday night, the main street was almost empty.

Surfers knew about the waves, but not many of them came. The road from Perth was long, and there was nowhere to stay. Surfers used to drive down on the weekend, sleep in their cars near the beach and cook dinner on a campfire. Back then, everybody in the water knew everybody's name.

Nowadays the town is very different. About fifty years ago, families started to grow grapes, and today there are a lot of wineries in the region. Tourists come for the wine, the food and the forest. Every year the best surfers in the world come here for a big professional contest, and the town is famous all over the world.

Some things haven't changed. The water is still cold, the waves are still big, and the locals still love them. Coach Dana Reid first came here with her family when she was twelve. "We used to sleep in a tent in the forest," she says. "Nowadays I bring a van full of surfers. But the first wave of the morning feels the same."
